risk_summary: This card payment of INR 1082.1 at a gaming merchant in Pune was made by a 60-year-old customer from Lucknow at 3:02 AM IST. The transaction triggered reason codes for a large customer-to-merchant distance (1177 km), night-time activity, and a high-risk merchant category (gaming). However, the device is not new to the customer, no recent failures or fraud history is linked to this device or customer, and the transaction risk score is low at 0.061766.

reason_codes.description: Unusual observed city or customer to merchant distance above 500 km
reason_codes.evidence: customer to merchant distance is 1177.08 km, exceeding 500 km threshold

reason_codes.description: Authorisation requested between midnight and 05:00 IST
reason_codes.evidence: transaction time is 3:02 AM IST, between midnight and 5 AM

reason_codes.description: Elevated category flag (gaming, gift_cards or electronics) under the synthetic teaching policy
reason_codes.evidence: merchant category is gaming, which is flagged as high risk

graph_findings: The device is used solely by this customer with no known fraud linked to it, and the customer has no own known fraud. The merchant has had one known fraud in the last 90 days, but this customer has only one previous payment in the same category and no fraud history.

recommended_action.rationale: The risk score is well below the 0.30 medium cutoff and no hard rules fired, so policy allows the payment (DOC_regulatory_exercises_0000799::2). The geographic distance alone is not sufficient for blocking as per NPCI guidance to consider travel or contextual changes (DOC_regulatory_exercises_0000342::0). Night activity is contextual evidence but not proof of fraud (DOC_regulatory_exercises_0000388::0).

cited_sources.document_title: Synthetic NPCI topic exercise 0342 on location change
cited_sources.used_for: contextualizing geographic distance reason code and location change
cited_sources.text:
Purpose:
Teach evidence-based review of location change for a fictional quick_commerce merchant. This exercise uses net_banking activity associated with Bengaluru; scenario variant 342. The exercise is part of a synthetic corpus, with no official status.

Context:
A payment arrives with incomplete history and an apparent contextual change. The reviewer must compare the current event with past observations. Compare city novelty with distance and ordinary travel. Do not block solely because customer and merchant cities differ.

cited_sources.used_for: explaining night activity reason code as contextual evidence
cited_sources.text:
Purpose:
Teach evidence-based review of night activity for a fictional other merchant. This exercise uses net_banking activity associated with Jaipur; scenario variant 388. The exercise is part of a synthetic corpus, with no official status.

Context:
A payment arrives with incomplete history and an apparent contextual change. The reviewer must compare the current event with past observations. Derive the hour in IST from an offset-aware timestamp. Night activity is contextual evidence, not proof.

cited_sources.document_title: Synthetic RBI topic exercise 0799 on access review
cited_sources.text:
Teaching policy:
The project starts with probability cutoffs 0.30, 0.60 and 0.85. Below 0.60 the policy allows the payment; from 0.60 to below 0.85 it requests review; at or above 0.85 it blocks. A blocklisted device takes precedence over a customer allowlist. These are client-provided starting settings, not a regulatory standard.
